scenes.title: Turn your idea into a buildable agreement
scenes.accessibleDescription: The capstone tests how you lead the process, not how quickly you ship an app.

scenes.title: Capture the idea, then agree on the journey
scenes.accessibleDescription: A structured readback turns your raw context into observable behavior.

scenes.title: Research reality and preserve decisions
scenes.accessibleDescription: Your package should distinguish evidence, plans, and uncertainty.

scenes.title: Map the system, then specify behavior
scenes.accessibleDescription: Trace success and failure before turning the design into a contract.

scenes.title: Prepare the kickoff and the long-run limits
scenes.accessibleDescription: Organize work before handing it to an execution agent.

scenes.title: Let a cold reader challenge the package
scenes.accessibleDescription: The reader should not need to reconstruct the original conversation.

scenes.title: Choose a scope you can actually explain
scenes.accessibleDescription: A small project gives the workflow enough substance without unnecessary breadth.

scenes.title: Assess the mirror, not the agent’s confidence
scenes.accessibleDescription: The agreed statement should preserve your intent and reveal suggestions.

scenes.title: Trace the diagram with your finger
scenes.accessibleDescription: A simple diagram should make responsibilities and recovery visible.

scenes.title: Ask how three requirements will be proven
scenes.accessibleDescription: Acceptance criteria should resolve differing interpretations.

scenes.title: Make the next safe action obvious
scenes.accessibleDescription: The final kickoff and handoff must work for a reader who starts cold.

scenes.title: Use review to improve the package
scenes.accessibleDescription: Keep the useful lessons while distinguishing simulation from observation.

scenes.title: Leave the understanding with the work
scenes.accessibleDescription: A transfer note preserves the decisions and identifies what must be rechecked.
